name: James P. Sullivan
note: A two-time Olympian who won the international mile championship in London in 1908, Sullivan took over the Stevens track team in 1914 and put it through practice three afternoons a week — a big step up in structure for the program. He brought along a famous training partner, too: his personal friend Johnny Hayes, the 1908 Olympic marathon gold medalist, pitched in with coaching and agreed to officiate the home meets.
research_note: Two-time Olympian and international mile champion, hired as coach; marathoner Johnny Hayes assisted. Only two mentions found in the archive pass, both from 1914 (pre-1920s deck, slides 54, 57) — tenure length beyond 1914 is unconfirmed, not verified as ending or continuing. Please verify against the full transcription/Link yearbook if possible.

name: Al McGall
note: A Stevens alumnus from the class of 1907, McGall returned to campus in 1916 to coach track and quickly became the program's utility man — he also led the school's undefeated 1917 football team on the side. In 1919 he launched Stevens' first cross country squad from scratch, running practices himself and telling would-be quitters exactly what he thought of their excuses: he kept a running list of the alibis he'd already heard ("I have no wind," "I am too heavy," "I am not heavy enough") and promised to tell any man straight whether he had what it took.
research_note: Stevens alumnus (class of 1907) returning as coach; also credited with leading the undefeated 1917 football team in a later mention. Name spelled inconsistently across clippings — 'McGall', 'McGill', and 'MacGill' all appear — confirm the correct spelling. Mentions run 1916-05-04 through 1919-11-12 (pre-1920s deck, slides 75, 80, 82, 84, 100/110, 111, 115); end_year is the last mention found, not a confirmed departure date.

name: J. E. Mitchell
note: Mitchell took over the track team in the fall of 1921, running the winter season while longtime coach "Doc" Davis focused on basketball. His tenure ended on a hard note: in February 1924, mounting financial deficits and a wave of academic ineligibility forced the Athletic Board to drop track as a full varsity sport. Mitchell stayed on afterward to piece together relay teams for the Penn Relays and other invitationals, keeping the sport alive in a scaled-back form.
research_note: Explicit appointment announcement, 'MITCHELL, TRACK TEAM COACH' (20s-70s deck, slide 14, 1921-10-12). Last mention 1924-02-13 (slide 36); end_year is the last mention found, not a confirmed departure date.

name: Gingrich
note: A Stevens professor with a running background, Gingrich agreed to coach the school's first cross country team in 1929 after a group of students simply organized themselves and asked him to lead it — the sport had no official varsity backing at the time. He ran practices three days a week and lined up meets against Rutgers and Seton Hall, hoping to build on a promising debut season. By that November, though, the student paper was already asking what had become of the team, pinning the fade-out on thin turnout in a student body of over 400.
research_note: Only two clippings found, both fall 1929 (20s-70s deck, slides 59, 60), covering cross country practice — first name not given. Tenure is almost certainly longer than one season; the gap on either side of this entry likely reflects missing clippings, not a confirmed vacancy. Needs more research.

name: O'Keefe
note: When students petitioned to bring back cross country after years without a team, "Chief" O'Keefe — a nickname that stuck from his Navy rank — volunteered to coach and pitched the Athletic Council on some genuinely ambitious plans: intercollegiate meets at Van Cortlandt Park and, eventually, Madison Square Garden. The Council signed off in October 1943, and O'Keefe's runners debuted that fall against three other colleges, though he held the team back from full competition until they'd logged more practice miles.
research_note: Took over on the program's return after a discontinuation, per a 1943-10-06 Athletic Association Council vote to bring back the 'harrier' team (20s-70s deck, slides 80-83). First name not given in any clipping ('Mr. O'Keefe' / 'Chief O'Keefe'). Only four mentions found, all fall 1943.

name: Tom Triol
note: The "Stevens Track Club" was barely a club at all in early 1948 — no dues, no meetings, and by its own members' admission, "up to now, no activity." That changed when Tom Triol, a former champion high hurdler, offered to coach its runners through the indoor season. Under him the club ran time trials in the 220, 440, 880, and mile to fill out relay teams for intercollegiate meets, giving the sport a real foothold again after years of informal running.
research_note: Single mention found: 'Track Club Discussed in Letter' (20s-70s deck, slide 86, 1948-02-07). Sport and tenure length unconfirmed.

name: Frank Misar
note: Misar ran Stevens' first-ever Interclass Track Meet in the spring of 1953, open to any student not already playing baseball, lacrosse, or tennis. When student interest sagged ahead of the event, he told the school paper flatly that its success was "solely in the hands of the student body" — not exactly a pep talk, but it got the point across. No coach is mentioned in the archive again for over two decades after him.
research_note: Single mention found: 'Attention, Speedsters!!!' (20s-70s deck, slide 89, 1953-04-25). Sport and tenure length unconfirmed. No further coach mentioned in the archive until Jim Lloyd in 1974 — a roughly 21-year dormant gap in the record.

name: Jim Lloyd
note: A Stevens alumnus (class of 1970) working in the college's Metallurgy Department, Lloyd revived cross country as a club sport in 1974 after a long dormant stretch — and then laced up alongside the runners he coached. He ran the Philadelphia Marathon with his own team that December, finishing in 3:37, and lined up again for the Asbury Park Marathon the following January, dropping out at mile 17 with a leg injury next to one of his own runners.
research_note: Revived cross country as a club sport after the long dormant period. Mentions run 1974-10-25 through 1975-10-24 (70s deck, slides 6-11). Also appears as 'Jim Loyd' once — likely an OCR/typo variant.

name: Bill Grothe
note: When Stevens elevated cross country to a full varsity sport in 1981 — after six years as a club team — Bill Grothe took over as its first official coach. By day he ran the college's financial aid office (he later became Registrar); by fall afternoons he built a program that quietly became one of the winningest at Stevens, trailing only the men's tennis team in win percentage over his tenure. He also inherited a ready-made star: junior Al Alonso, who had already helped push the sport to varsity status and would go on to succeed him as coach.
research_note: Hired as first-year coach when cross country was elevated to varsity; headline 'Coach Named' (80s deck, slides 16-17, 1981-08-28). Also named Athletic Director around the same time. Also appears as 'William Grothe'. Last mention 1984-08-26 (slide 47); Al Alonso's first mention as coach follows just weeks later (1984-09-14), suggesting a clean handoff.

name: Al Alonso
role: Head Coach, Cross Country & Track and Field
note: The program's longest-tenured coach by far, Alonso took over cross country in 1984 — just a year after graduating from Stevens himself, where he'd been the driving force behind getting the sport promoted to varsity and had led the team to an IAC title in 1982. He added the head track job by the mid-1990s, and in 1995 coached Stevens' first-ever full women's track & field team, a season that earned the program NCAA All-American recognition. He was still coaching as of the archive's final batch in 2000, by then working alongside assistant coach Tom Zapata.
research_note: Longest-tenured coach on record — first mention as coach 1984-09-14 (80s deck, slide 50), still coaching as of the archive's last batch (2000-11-17). Started as cross country coach; by 1995 also referred to as 'Head Track' coach ('Track & Field Team Finishes High', 90s deck, slide 43), so track & field appears to have been added at some point in between — exact year not confirmed. Full name 'Adalberto Alonso' is used increasingly in later clippings; 'Al Alonzo' appears once (1996-04-12), likely a typo. Was also a record-setting Stevens athlete 1980-88 before becoming coach — see the matching entry in alumni.json. An assistant coach, Tom Zapata, appears in a 2000 roster clipping (slide 14). end_year is null because the archive ends in 2000 with no departure reported, not because the tenure is confirmed to extend past 2000.
